# Compliance tooling

The compliance package turns evidence from CI into control states and the assessor package. These tools read and check its documents: they validate the OSCAL files against the published schema, import the published control catalogues, and confirm that a second OSCAL tool can open the package. None of them runs in the product.

Back to the [component catalogue](./index.md).

## npm:ajv

**What it provides.** Validates OSCAL documents and the compliance package's own JSON sources against their schemas.

**Why it is needed.** Checks every OSCAL document, and the compliance package's own JSON files, against their schemas, offline. Without it a malformed control document could reach an assessor package. A JSON Schema validator of our own would be large and easy to get wrong.

## npm:ajv-formats

**What it provides.** String formats (dates, URIs) for the ajv validation.

**Why it is needed.** Adds the date, date-time and URI checks the OSCAL schema uses. Without it ajv would skip those checks.

## npm:parse5

**What it provides.** Parses the published Cyber Centre and other control-catalogue HTML when importing catalogues.

**Why it is needed.** Parses the published control catalogue web pages, such as the Cyber Centre's ITSG-33 pages, when the catalogues are imported. A parser that follows the HTML standard avoids fragile pattern matching on web pages.

## npm:yaml

**What it provides.** Reads YAML sources (workflow files and imported data) in the compliance tooling.

**Why it is needed.** Reads YAML in the compliance tooling: workflow files and imported data such as the CISO Assistant cross-check. Node.js has no YAML parser built in.

## tool:oscal-cli

**What it provides.** Validates and resolves the OSCAL content in CI and the release package (owner-approved 2026-11-21).

**Why it is needed.** The reference OSCAL tool. It validates every OSCAL document and resolves the profiles, in CI and for the release package. It is an independent second check, beside ajv, that the assessor package is valid OSCAL.
